## Project Summary – The Explorers That Never Came Home

**The Explorers That Never Came Home** is an interactive, comic-style NASA space exploration flipbook that tells the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments that remained in space after completing their missions. The project covers famous missions such as Apollo, Spirit and Opportunity, Sojourner, Viking, Dawn, Pioneer, Ingenuity, and Kepler.

The project combines 15 pages of illustrated storytelling with an English audio narration to make complex space science more engaging and easier to understand. It addresses the challenge of making scientific information accessible and interesting, especially for students and young space enthusiasts.

This project is important because it highlights the achievements of NASA's past missions, explains their scientific contributions, and inspires curiosity about space exploration. It also demonstrates how digital storytelling and multimedia technology can transform educational content into an interactive learning experience.

1. What does the project do?
It is a 15-page comic-style digital flipbook that explains the stories of NASA spacecraft, landers, and rovers left behind after completing their missions. It includes illustrations and audio narration.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Makes space science interesting and easy to understand.
  • Helps students learn about NASA missions.
  • Combines storytelling, visuals, and audio.
  • Encourages interest in science and technology.

3. What is its intended impact?
To create awareness about space exploration and inspire students to learn more about science and technology.

4. What tools and software were used?

  • Heyzine – Digital flipbook creation.
  • PowerPoint – Presentation design.
  • PDF – Content organisation.
  • Audio tools – Narration.
  • NASA websites – Research and information.

5. How is the project creative?
It presents real space missions through comic-style storytelling, colourful illustrations, and audio narration instead of traditional text.
